 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.1493 Of 2010

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The revision petitioner was convicted in CC.No.408 of 2003 on the file of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, godavarikhani, vide Judgemnt dated 27.07.2007, for the offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code for the reason of cheating PWs.1 to 7 by taking Rs. 9,40,000/- on the promise that they would be made partners in the business and the amount would be invested.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, godavarikhani
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, the said amount was taken, but, PWs.1 to 7 were not made as partners.
Aggrieved by the said conduct, a criminal complaint was filed against the accused.
It is alleged that PWs.1 to 7, in all, gave an amount of Rs.9,40,000/- and the accused issued Exs.P2 to P8 receipts in favour of PWs.1 to 7.
The said amount was sought to be invested in a TV show room that would be started by the accused.
2. The learned trial Judge examined PWs.1 to 7 and also the owner of the premises where the accused was doing business.
Further, the handwriting expert PW11 gave opinion that the receipts Exs.P2 to P8 were signed by the accused.
On the basis of the evidence, the learned trial Judge convicted the accused for the offence under Section 420 of the IPC and sentenced him to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of one year.

3. The said conviction when questioned in appeal before the Sessions Court in Crl.A.No.15 of 2008,
the learned Sessions Judge vide Judgment dated 03.02.2009 found that the evidence of PWs.1 to 7 regarding handing over the money corroborated with the evidence of PW11-handwriting expert that the receipts Exs.P2 P8 were executed by the accused.

Further, there was no cross- examination of PW11-hand writing expert which implies that the accused in fact accepted the issuance of receipts Exs.P2 to P8.
4.

Learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner would submit that the disputes if any are purely civil in nature since they arose out of differences regarding the investment and making PWs.1 to 7 as partners in the business being run by accused.
The remedy if any would be before the Civil Court and there is no element of criminality to convict the revision petitioner/accused for the offence under Section 420 of the IPC.
5. Admittedly, the accused was running business in the premises of PW10.
He had promised that he would make PWs.1 to 7 as partners in his business and had taken the amount of Rs.9,40,000/- by executing receipts.
From the subsequent conduct it can be infered that the accused had the intention to cheat PWs.1 to 7 from the inception of the transaction.
Having made false promise of inducting PWs.1 to 7 as partners in his business, he has taken the amount.

The ingredients of Section 420 of IPC for making false representation and thereby taking the amounts, which amounts were given by PWs.1 to 7 believing the version of accused satisfies the ingredients of Section 420 of IPC.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel alternatively argues that the sentence of imprisonment may be considered to be set off, since the petitioner is now aged more than 55 years and have dependents to look after.
Further, there are no other criminal antecedents insofar as the accused is concerned.
Learned Public Prosecutor does not dispute the factum of accused not having any criminal antecedents.

7. Since the transaction is of the year 2003, and nearly 21 years have passed by, this Court deems it appropriate to reduce the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner/accused.
8. Accordingly, Criminal Revision Case is partly allowed.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
